bull_bear.body: - Asset-light philosophy maintained; no significant debt. Cash conserved and recycled into own IPP projects and bank margin requirements. IPP kept small intentionally so EPC stays dominant.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Flat/soft order inflow** vs strong industry tailwind — the central concern; FY27 top-line growth not visible if book just gets replenished, not grown.
- **Grid evacuation / substation clarity**: CTUIL/CERC (10-Apr order) flagged ~60 GW RE in Rajasthan awaiting substation coordinate clarity. Mgmt says EPC only awarded after developer secures land + connectivity, so current 2.8 GW book unaffected — but this could slow NEW EPC awards (risk pushed onto developers/inflow).
- **ALCM module-cost regulation**: cost per watt INR 14 → INR 23 expected (enforcement ~Jun-1-2026) — mgmt says fully pass-through, neutral to WAAREERTL.
- Working-capital expansion (receivables/inventory) — needs FY27 normalization confirmation.
- Customer/state concentration (Rajasthan heavy). Land acquisition is a developer-side challenge (not directly WAAREERTL's, but gates inflow).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - CFO Sharma confident on execution/margins but **notably evasive/repetitive** on quantitative asks (order-book value, hit-ratio, BESS cost, module mix, FY27 guidance) — answers default to "depends on the quarter/order." Tone disciplined and conservative (15% margin anchoring, asset-light insistence). Analysts (Axis, Anand Rathi, Sapphire) pressed hard on inflow softness and grid risk; mgmt acknowledged but did not fully resolve.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- Headline Q4 +131% revenue is **flattered by the 50% with-module mix** (a low-margin pass-through-heavy revenue boost) — underlying MW execution actually *declined* (H1 ~700-900 MW/qtr to <500-600 in Q4). Revenue growth ≠ execution growth this quarter.
- Order book DOWN YoY despite record execution = the franchise is running to stand still on backlog; growth hinges on converting the 36 GW bilateral pipeline, which is unquantified.
- Domestic supply chain insulated them from oil/gas-shock and LPG/labour disruption — a defensive positive.
- BESS is the cleanest near-term optionality (revenue opens FY27); data-center is hype-stage only.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Comprehensive end-to-end solar EPC capability spanning engineering, procurement, construction, T&D, testing and commissioning, allowing single-point accountability
- Supported by a strong parent company (Waaree Energies Limited), enabling seamless integration with its module manufacturing business and an ecosystem play within the group
- Large order book of 2,832 MWp backed by a proven track record — 2,727 MWp executed during FY 2025-26 and a 5.06 GWp cumulative solar EPC portfolio
- Asset-light business model underpinning robust growth and financial performance
- Bankable EPC provider with marquee clientele including Greenko, Jindal Renewables, Acciona, NEEPCO, Continuum, AM Green and DRPL
- In-house design and engineering team with an India-based cost-effective structure, plus an in-house R&D team for new technology development
- 3-stage quality assurance process — initial factory assessment, production monitoring at vendor facility, and final pre-shipment inspection — with centralised field quality monitoring
- Credit rating upgraded to A+ Stable (CARE) during FY 2025-26, following an earlier upgrade to A Stable, supporting project financing credibility
- Recurring O&M portfolio of ~1,180 MWp providing lifecycle revenue beyond construction
- Expertise across all project sizes and formats — utility-scale ground-mounted, rooftop, floating solar and BESS
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Single-activity concentration in solar EPC — The Company's business is entirely turnkey solar EPC for renewable energy projects, with construction and maintenance of power plants accounting for 100% of business activity and 98.52% of turnover. There is no product or activity diversification to absorb a downturn in solar EPC ordering or margins.
- Order-book dependence and execution concentration — Near-term visibility rests on a 2,832 MWp unexecuted order book and a bidding pipeline; revenue is contract-driven rather than recurring, so slippage in conversion, commissioning or client project timelines translates directly into revenue risk.
- Customer concentration in a small number of large utility-scale projects — A large share of the portfolio sits in a handful of GW-scale contracts — Jindal Renewables (2,012.47 MWp), Greenko (980 MWp), NEEPCO (450 MWp) and Acciona (412 MWp) — so the loss, delay or renegotiation of any single marquee contract is material to the overall book.
- Group and parent dependence — The Company describes itself as supported by a strong parent company enabling seamless integration with its module manufacturing business and an ecosystem play within the group; procurement and sales flow through group entities including the holding company Waaree Energies Limited, creating dependence on group supply, pricing and reputation.
- Geographic concentration in India with no export diversification — Operations span 11 states and 58 domestic locations with zero international locations and exports at 0% of turnover, leaving the Company fully exposed to Indian policy, tariff, auction and land/evacuation conditions with no offshore offset.
- High employee attrition and a thin permanent workforce — Permanent-employee turnover was 28.69% in FY 2025-26 (30.25% male, 12.70% female), up from 27.22% in FY 2024-25 and 18.73% in FY 2023-24, against only 399 permanent employees; sustained attrition at this level in an execution-intensive engineering business threatens delivery capability.
- Reliance on contract and non-permanent labour — Of 795 total employees, 396 are other-than-permanent and the Company reports zero permanent workers, so project delivery depends on a contingent workforce whose availability, cost and safety performance the Company controls less directly.
- Forward-looking statement risk flagged by the Board — The Board's cautionary statement warns that objectives, projections, estimates and expectations constitute forward-looking statements and that actual results might differ materially depending on market conditions and circumstances.

outlook.body: WRTL's expansion in FY 2025-26 was project- and adjacency-led rather than plant-led, consistent with its asset-light EPC model. The Company executed 2,727 MWp of projects during the year and carried an unexecuted order book of 2,832 MWp at March 31, 2026, with a cumulative solar EPC portfolio of 5.06 GWp. Major projects under execution or commissioned include a 2 GWp solar project for Jindal Renewables at Bikaner, Rajasthan (described as India's largest single-location capacity), 980 MWp for Greenko as part of the Pinnapuram Integrated Renewable Energy Storage Project at Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh, the 412.5 MWp Acciona ISTS project at Bikaner commissioned during FY 2025-26, and a 1.2 MWp floating solar project for Rubamin in Gujarat. Ground-mounted project clusters span Bikaner (2,897 MWp), Solapur (1,217.5 MWp), Jamnagar (305 MWp), Tuticorin (180 MWp), Ratlam (150 MWp), Nashik (131 MWp), Kasdol (78 MWp), Simhapuri (52.6 MWp), Kadapa (39.8 MWp) and Yavatmal (29.4 MWp). Beyond EPC, the Company is building out its own asset base: an operational IPP portfolio of 54.82 MWp with a further 227.10 MWp under construction, a commissioned rooftop portfolio of 59.26 MWp, 2.29 MWp of commissioned floating solar, and an O&M portfolio of approximately 1,180 MWp. New verticals added during the year include BESS EPC, with 90 MWh under execution at Jaisalmer, Rajasthan and a 1,520 MWh battery energy storage system order recorded in 2026, alongside T&D EPC and Data Centre EPC. Inorganic expansion comprised the incorporation of Sunsational Power Private Limited as a wholly owned subsidiary on May 20, 2025, a minority investment in Smart Joules Private Limited taking the Company to 3.23% on a fully diluted basis, and completion of the acquisition of a 55% equity stake in Associated Power Structures Private Limited (APSPL) with effect from June 18, 2026, which supports the move into transmission and distribution infrastructure. Nationally the Company operated 23 EPC and 34 O&M project locations plus one office across 11 states, with no international locations.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's energy landscape is moving through a structural shift as renewable energy becomes central to future capacity creation, energy security and economic growth, with solar leading the transition.
- The transition is creating a broader renewable ecosystem beyond generation — storage, grid integration, O&M and asset management are becoming critical, favouring partners with scale, execution discipline and end-to-end capabilities.
- As solar's share increases, demand for efficient EPC execution, dependable O&M services and integrated clean energy solutions is expected to deepen, expanding beyond utility-scale into commercial, industrial and rooftop applications.
- The opportunity is expanding beyond project construction into BESS, T&D, O&M and asset management; as the market matures, execution capability, cost discipline and integrated service offerings will become key differentiators.
- Government policy is a decisive driver — the Solar Parks Scheme (extended to FY 2028-29), PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, and the PLI Scheme for solar PV manufacturing are strengthening project viability and creating a clearer pathway for long-term solar capacity addition.
- BESS is gaining momentum through focused policy support, with ISTS transmission charge waivers available for co-located BESS projects commissioned until June 2028 for a period of 12 years.
- Transmission infrastructure expansion supports the T&D adjacency — the National Electricity Plan (Transmission) targets addition of approximately 4.9 lakh circuit kilometres of transmission lines during FY 2027-32, and Green Energy Corridor Phase III & IV are expected to facilitate evacuation of nearly 150 GW of renewable capacity.
- India's structural transformation is driven by long-term policy support, cost competitiveness, energy security priorities and decarbonisation imperatives rather than short-term cyclical demand, with green hydrogen, hybrid solar-wind systems and large-scale battery storage emerging as the defining pillars of the next phase of growth.
- Grid integration, permitting delays and financing gaps, especially in emerging economies, remain the key hurdles to sustaining momentum.
- FY 2025-26 momentum was driven by strong project delivery, disciplined cost management and sustained demand in the solar EPC market, with a healthy order book and strong bidding pipeline providing near-term visibility.
- The unexecuted order book of the Company stands at 2,832 MWp as at March 31, 2026, having grown from 817 MWp in 2023, 2,365 MWp in 2024 and 3,263 MWp in 2025.
- The Company completed 2,727 MWp of project execution during FY 2025-26, supported by disciplined project management and scalable operating capabilities.
- New orders received during FY 2025-26 amounted to 2,322.3 MWp.
- The execution timeline for the current unexecuted order book is 12-15 months.
- The bidding pipeline stands at 36 GWp, spanning government, private utility-scale and commercial segments.
- The order book is structured to support efficient execution over a defined delivery horizon, with project types, contract structures and geographic concentration aligned to execution certainty and operational efficiency.
- Cumulative solar EPC portfolio of 5.06 GWp and an O&M portfolio of ~1,180 MWp; under-execution BESS EPC portfolio of 90 MWh; IPP portfolio of 54.82 MWp operational with 227.10 MWp under construction.

currentContext.expansion: WRTL's expansion in FY 2025-26 was project- and adjacency-led rather than plant-led, consistent with its asset-light EPC model. The Company executed 2,727 MWp of projects during the year and carried an unexecuted order book of 2,832 MWp at March 31, 2026, with a cumulative solar EPC portfolio of 5.06 GWp. Major projects under execution or commissioned include a 2 GWp solar project for Jindal Renewables at Bikaner, Rajasthan (described as India's largest single-location capacity), 980 MWp for Greenko as part of the Pinnapuram Integrated Renewable Energy Storage Project at Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh, the 412.5 MWp Acciona ISTS project at Bikaner commissioned during FY 2025-26, and a 1.2 MWp floating solar project for Rubamin in Gujarat. Ground-mounted project clusters span Bikaner (2,897 MWp), Solapur (1,217.5 MWp), Jamnagar (305 MWp), Tuticorin (180 MWp), Ratlam (150 MWp), Nashik (131 MWp), Kasdol (78 MWp), Simhapuri (52.6 MWp), Kadapa (39.8 MWp) and Yavatmal (29.4 MWp). Beyond EPC, the Company is building out its own asset base: an operational IPP portfolio of 54.82 MWp with a further 227.10 MWp under construction, a commissioned rooftop portfolio of 59.26 MWp, 2.29 MWp of commissioned floating solar, and an O&M portfolio of approximately 1,180 MWp. New verticals added during the year include BESS EPC, with 90 MWh under execution at Jaisalmer, Rajasthan and a 1,520 MWh battery energy storage system order recorded in 2026, alongside T&D EPC and Data Centre EPC. Inorganic expansion comprised the incorporation of Sunsational Power Private Limited as a wholly owned subsidiary on May 20, 2025, a minority investment in Smart Joules Private Limited taking the Company to 3.23% on a fully diluted basis, and completion of the acquisition of a 55% equity stake in Associated Power Structures Private Limited (APSPL) with effect from June 18, 2026, which supports the move into transmission and distribution infrastructure. Nationally the Company operated 23 EPC and 34 O&M project locations plus one office across 11 states, with no international locations.

one-line thesis: Pure-play, asset-light solar EPC compounder riding India's ~44 GW/yr solar additions, posting ~108% FY26 revenue/PAT growth with ~19% EBITDA margins (vs 15% guided floor), but the watch-item is flat-to-soft order INFLOW (2.3 GW vs 2.4 GW) capping FY27 growth visibility despite a fat 36 GW bilateral pipeline.

**One-offs / quality flags:** Q4 realization spiked to ~INR 20 mn/MW because ~50% of Q4 execution revenue was "with-module" (vs normal ~10-20% module mix) — mgmt confirmed this is an **aberration**, not recurring. Working capital stretched: trade receivables more than doubled (~500 to >double) and inventory up — mgmt says receivables <6 months, many LC-backed, no govt payment stretch; inventory is project-specific. OCF conversion weaker YoY (cash redeployed into IPP capex / bank margin money). Big jump in non-current "other financial assets" = GST receivables with govt + supplier advances.
guidance (incl. next quarter):
- No hard revenue/MW guidance given for FY27; mgmt repeatedly deflected. Order book 2.8 GW executes over ~12–15 months; FY27 = existing book + new orders won during the year.
- **EBITDA margin floor guided at ~15%** ("threshold/guiding number"), but mgmt insists operational discipline keeps delivery sustainably >19% and won't necessarily "normalize down."
- BESS EPC revenue stream "will open up during the current financial year" (FY27) — first small BESS project under execution now.
- 227 MWp additional IPP to be commissioned during FY27.
order book & pipeline:
- Order book 2.83 GWp (down from 3.2 GW YoY); FY26 inflow ~2.3 GW vs ~2.4 GW prior (~5% dip — mgmt vague on cause: mix of negotiation lead-time + possible competition, "difficult to quantify").
- Pipeline ~36 GW being chased bilaterally: ~23 GW domestic + ~12 GW international. Hit-ratio undisclosed ("bilateral, difficult to quantify").
- Order economics: ~INR 1.0–1.25 cr/MW (varies hugely with module/BOS/turnkey scope). ~7-8 states; **Rajasthan is the heavyweight**, plus Gujarat, MP, Andhra, Maharashtra.
- No overseas execution yet; overseas pipeline being chased.
segment / subsidiary:
- Three revenue streams: EPC + O&M + IPP. EPC dominant; O&M = recurring base (1.18 GW); IPP deliberately kept small.
- Subsidiary of Waaree Energies (module parent). Modules sourced arms-length from parent OR third parties depending on customer — no fixed parent split.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **BESS EPC**: real but early — one small project executing, "lot of inquiries" alongside solar; can drive battery cost if customer orders battery from them. Incremental BESS cost guessed ~0.5–0.75 (per MW) depending on scope.
- **Data centers**: inquiry-stage only, no firm order, no revenue — optionality not yet monetized.
- IPP build-out (54 MW + 227 MW) for 20–25 yr annuity revenue, but explicitly "very less" % of total revenue.
margins & cost dynamics:
- FY26 EBITDA margin 19.24%, sustained YoY (FY25 also >19%). Quarterly margin swings with customer mix. All contracts fixed-price; module price rises fully passed through to customer (turnkey priced at prevailing rate, procured immediately).
- Pure-EPC vs turnkey: same margin-threshold approach, no segment is structurally higher/lower margin.
capex / expansion:
- IPP capex: ~INR 3–3.5 cr/MWp for solar install; 227 MW addition implies several hundred cr, **funded entirely via internal accruals — no debt tied up**. CWIP on balance sheet reflects this.
- 120 MW IPP referenced earlier (~INR 3.5 cr/MW ≈ INR 420 cr) — internal-accrual funded.
capital allocation: - Asset-light philosophy maintained; no significant debt. Cash conserved and recycled into own IPP projects and bank margin requirements. IPP kept small intentionally so EPC stays dominant.
risks & watch-items:
- **Flat/soft order inflow** vs strong industry tailwind — the central concern; FY27 top-line growth not visible if book just gets replenished, not grown.
- **Grid evacuation / substation clarity**: CTUIL/CERC (10-Apr order) flagged ~60 GW RE in Rajasthan awaiting substation coordinate clarity. Mgmt says EPC only awarded after developer secures land + connectivity, so current 2.8 GW book unaffected — but this could slow NEW EPC awards (risk pushed onto developers/inflow).
- **ALCM module-cost regulation**: cost per watt INR 14 → INR 23 expected (enforcement ~Jun-1-2026) — mgmt says fully pass-through, neutral to WAAREERTL.
- Working-capital expansion (receivables/inventory) — needs FY27 normalization confirmation.
- Customer/state concentration (Rajasthan heavy). Land acquisition is a developer-side challenge (not directly WAAREERTL's, but gates inflow).
management quality / tone: - CFO Sharma confident on execution/margins but **notably evasive/repetitive** on quantitative asks (order-book value, hit-ratio, BESS cost, module mix, FY27 guidance) — answers default to "depends on the quarter/order." Tone disciplined and conservative (15% margin anchoring, asset-light insistence). Analysts (Axis, Anand Rathi, Sapphire) pressed hard on inflow softness and grid risk; mgmt acknowledged but did not fully resolve.
non-obvious takeaways:
- Headline Q4 +131% revenue is **flattered by the 50% with-module mix** (a low-margin pass-through-heavy revenue boost) — underlying MW execution actually *declined* (H1 ~700-900 MW/qtr to <500-600 in Q4). Revenue growth ≠ execution growth this quarter.
- Order book DOWN YoY despite record execution = the franchise is running to stand still on backlog; growth hinges on converting the 36 GW bilateral pipeline, which is unquantified.
- Domestic supply chain insulated them from oil/gas-shock and LPG/labour disruption — a defensive positive.
- BESS is the cleanest near-term optionality (revenue opens FY27); data-center is hype-stage only.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's energy landscape is moving through a structural shift as renewable energy becomes central to future capacity creation, energy security and economic growth, with solar leading the transition.
- The transition is creating a broader renewable ecosystem beyond generation — storage, grid integration, O&M and asset management are becoming critical, favouring partners with scale, execution discipline and end-to-end capabilities.
- As solar's share increases, demand for efficient EPC execution, dependable O&M services and integrated clean energy solutions is expected to deepen, expanding beyond utility-scale into commercial, industrial and rooftop applications.
- The opportunity is expanding beyond project construction into BESS, T&D, O&M and asset management; as the market matures, execution capability, cost discipline and integrated service offerings will become key differentiators.
- Government policy is a decisive driver — the Solar Parks Scheme (extended to FY 2028-29), PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, and the PLI Scheme for solar PV manufacturing are strengthening project viability and creating a clearer pathway for long-term solar capacity addition.
- BESS is gaining momentum through focused policy support, with ISTS transmission charge waivers available for co-located BESS projects commissioned until June 2028 for a period of 12 years.
- Transmission infrastructure expansion supports the T&D adjacency — the National Electricity Plan (Transmission) targets addition of approximately 4.9 lakh circuit kilometres of transmission lines during FY 2027-32, and Green Energy Corridor Phase III & IV are expected to facilitate evacuation of nearly 150 GW of renewable capacity.
- India's structural transformation is driven by long-term policy support, cost competitiveness, energy security priorities and decarbonisation imperatives rather than short-term cyclical demand, with green hydrogen, hybrid solar-wind systems and large-scale battery storage emerging as the defining pillars of the next phase of growth.
- Grid integration, permitting delays and financing gaps, especially in emerging economies, remain the key hurdles to sustaining momentum.
- FY 2025-26 momentum was driven by strong project delivery, disciplined cost management and sustained demand in the solar EPC market, with a healthy order book and strong bidding pipeline providing near-term visibility.
- The unexecuted order book of the Company stands at 2,832 MWp as at March 31, 2026, having grown from 817 MWp in 2023, 2,365 MWp in 2024 and 3,263 MWp in 2025.
- The Company completed 2,727 MWp of project execution during FY 2025-26, supported by disciplined project management and scalable operating capabilities.
- New orders received during FY 2025-26 amounted to 2,322.3 MWp.
- The execution timeline for the current unexecuted order book is 12-15 months.
- The bidding pipeline stands at 36 GWp, spanning government, private utility-scale and commercial segments.
- The order book is structured to support efficient execution over a defined delivery horizon, with project types, contract structures and geographic concentration aligned to execution certainty and operational efficiency.
- Cumulative solar EPC portfolio of 5.06 GWp and an O&M portfolio of ~1,180 MWp; under-execution BESS EPC portfolio of 90 MWh; IPP portfolio of 54.82 MWp operational with 227.10 MWp under construction.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: WRTL's expansion in FY 2025-26 was project- and adjacency-led rather than plant-led, consistent with its asset-light EPC model. The Company executed 2,727 MWp of projects during the year and carried an unexecuted order book of 2,832 MWp at March 31, 2026, with a cumulative solar EPC portfolio of 5.06 GWp. Major projects under execution or commissioned include a 2 GWp solar project for Jindal Renewables at Bikaner, Rajasthan (described as India's largest single-location capacity), 980 MWp for Greenko as part of the Pinnapuram Integrated Renewable Energy Storage Project at Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh, the 412.5 MWp Acciona ISTS project at Bikaner commissioned during FY 2025-26, and a 1.2 MWp floating solar project for Rubamin in Gujarat. Ground-mounted project clusters span Bikaner (2,897 MWp), Solapur (1,217.5 MWp), Jamnagar (305 MWp), Tuticorin (180 MWp), Ratlam (150 MWp), Nashik (131 MWp), Kasdol (78 MWp), Simhapuri (52.6 MWp), Kadapa (39.8 MWp) and Yavatmal (29.4 MWp). Beyond EPC, the Company is building out its own asset base: an operational IPP portfolio of 54.82 MWp with a further 227.10 MWp under construction, a commissioned rooftop portfolio of 59.26 MWp, 2.29 MWp of commissioned floating solar, and an O&M portfolio of approximately 1,180 MWp. New verticals added during the year include BESS EPC, with 90 MWh under execution at Jaisalmer, Rajasthan and a 1,520 MWh battery energy storage system order recorded in 2026, alongside T&D EPC and Data Centre EPC. Inorganic expansion comprised the incorporation of Sunsational Power Private Limited as a wholly owned subsidiary on May 20, 2025, a minority investment in Smart Joules Private Limited taking the Company to 3.23% on a fully diluted basis, and completion of the acquisition of a 55% equity stake in Associated Power Structures Private Limited (APSPL) with effect from June 18, 2026, which supports the move into transmission and distribution infrastructure. Nationally the Company operated 23 EPC and 34 O&M project locations plus one office across 11 states, with no international locations.

themes.need: DISCOMs mandating firm/round-the-clock RE make BESS + pumped-hydro the bid differentiator, and in Q1FY27 storage demand ran ahead of supply. ADANIGREEN has 3.5 GWh of BESS installed (+1.9 GWh at Khavda this quarter), targets 10+ GWh this fiscal and 50 GWh by FY30 on a thumb-rule INR 25-30 lakh of EBITDA per MWh against ~INR 1.5cr/MWh of capex, and has contracted essentially all merchant/C&I capacity to sibling AESL on 25-year (solar/wind) and 15-year (battery) fixed-price PPAs targeting ~15-16% IRR - a pivot from merchant builder to fixed-return contracted IPP, with evacuation (not panels) named as the binding constraint. JSWENERGY added 873 MW in Q1 and ~1.1 GW since April - 36% of its 3 GW FY27 target already banked, Tidong Hydro commissioned four months early - and raised INR 10,150cr, taking net leverage 5.2x to 4.95x. On the equipment side SERVOTECH said its BESS pack capacity is fully booked ('we are not able to meet the demand') and committed to 2x capacity in 6 months, 3x by 21-Mar-2027 and 10x within 2 years. ACMESOLAR/KPIGREEN/SUZLON/INOXWIND attach storage to solar/wind; NTPC/NHPC/SJVN/TATAPOWER drive pumped-hydro and utility-scale storage.
themes.driver: BESS capacity commissioning against demand two independent managements (ADANIGREEN, SERVOTECH) say already exceeds supply; FDRE/peak-power tender awards; merchant DAM prices (JSWENERGY: INR 4.40 -> INR 5.10/unit, +16%) on +8.5% Q1 power demand.
